_comment: English is the fallback catalog: any key missing from another language resolves here. Keys are dotted paths; field labels and help follow <prefix>.<field>.label / .help.
action.adoptHelp: The broker holds this but the bot has no record of it — adopt it to arm the scale-out ladder, the max-hold barrier and correct P&L tracking going forward. It only gets a plain stop-loss/take-profit until then.
action.forgetHelp: Already sold this by hand? Drop the bot's record without placing an order.
alloc.note: Share is of total equity (cash + holdings), the same denominator the limit divides by. A class at its cap refuses further BUYS, including topping up a position already held; sells and exits are never affected. Holdings nothing could classify are budgeted under "unclassified", which counts against no cap until you set one.
alloc.title: Allocation by asset class
auth.intro: This bot is protected by server.auth_token. Enter it to continue.
auth.rejected: The server rejected that token. Check server.auth_token in config.yaml.
auth.rememberHelp: Off, the token is kept only until this tab closes. Turn it on only on a device you control — anything with the token can place orders.
auth.title: API token required
banner.noAuth.body: server.auth_token is empty, so anything that can reach this port can place orders, cancel them and toggle live trading. Set a token before exposing this port beyond localhost.
banner.noAuth.title: ⚠️ This API is unauthenticated.
banner.risk.body: This software trades real money when connected to a live broker. The authors accept no responsibility for any financial losses. Automated strategies can and do lose money; backtested performance does not predict future results. Not financial advice.
banner.risk.title: ⚠️ USE AT YOUR OWN RISK.
chart.caption: {symbol}: {bars} bars, {decisions} decisions ({fills} filled). Green ▲ buys, red ▼ sells; hollow markers are dry-run or blocked decisions. Hover for OHLC.
chart.noSymbols: No symbols on the watchlist yet.
chart.sub: candles with this bot's own executions marked
chart.title: Price & trades
chrome.lockHelp: Forget the API token in this browser
common.noscript: This interface needs JavaScript for navigation. The JSON API is available at /api.
confirm.adopt:
Track {symbol} as an open position?

This places NO order — it only creates the bot's own record from what the broker already reports (quantity and average price). Entry time is set to now, since the real entry time is unknown; the scale-out ladder and max-hold barrier will measure from this point on.
confirm.disableTestMode: Ending test mode now switches ALL future orders back to the REAL broker immediately.
confirm.enableTrading: Enable automated trading? The bot will place real orders through the configured broker.
confirm.forget:
Remove {symbol} from the bot's open positions?

This places NO order — use it only if you already sold {symbol} yourself. It will not appear in realised P&L or the win/loss stats.

If you still hold it, press Cancel and use Sell instead.
confirm.restrictAutotune:
Restrict the scheduled auto-optimizer to ONLY {symbol}?

This is an allow-list, not a per-symbol flag: every OTHER watchlist symbol will stop being evaluated by autotune until this restriction is removed (from here, or from any other symbol also on the list).
confirm.resume:
Resume trading after the halt?

The drawdown peak is re-based to current equity, so the same drawdown will not immediately re-trip. Check why it halted first.
confirm.runAutotuneNow:
Run the auto-optimizer now, across every eligible watchlist symbol?

This writes straight into strategy_overrides and the running engine for any symbol that improves — the same unsupervised action a scheduled pass takes, just triggered right now instead of waiting for the next tick. No further confirmation per symbol.
dash.noActivity: Nothing has happened since this page was opened.
dash.noSignals: No signals yet — the strategy needs candle history to warm up.
dash.openSub: what the bot opened and still holds
diag.detectorsSub: status of the optional learned detectors
diag.errorsSub: recent failures from the data feed and broker
diag.protectionsSub: halt state, drawdown and symbol lockouts
msg.forgot: {symbol} removed from the bot's open positions.
opt.applyElsewhere: Set this on the Settings tab
opt.baselineLine: Baseline (current setting): return {return}, win {win}, {trades} trades, over {bars} cached bars.
opt.belowRecentWin: This symbol's real trading since autotune's own last change to it has been winning ({trades} trades, {win} win rate, {expectancy} expectancy per trade) — the winning candidate above doesn't beat that, so it was rejected. A config that's already working needs a real edge over its own recent record before it's replaced, not just a better-looking backtest.
opt.belowReturnFloor: The winning candidate's return ({return}) is below the minimum return floor ({floor}), so it was rejected regardless of anything else — see the row above for its full numbers. Adjusting the floor won't change what shows here: the search ranks candidates by Objective alone, unaware of this floor, so it always settles on the same candidate; the floor only decides whether that candidate is accepted. Try a different Objective, or lower the floor if a small loss is acceptable for this symbol.
opt.busy: Another sweep is already running — try again in a moment.
opt.improvedHint: "real" is this symbol's actual, capital-constrained track record; "what if fully capitalized" is today's config backtested in isolation with no competition for capital from the rest of the watchlist. A proposal is only marked best when it beats both — beating just one can mean it only wins against an unrealistic assumption, or only looks good because the real history is too thin to judge (a fresh symbol has none at all, and is judged on "what if" alone).
opt.intro: Backtests one field at a time against a watchlist symbol's cached history, holding everything else at its current setting — the interactive sibling of `optimize -sensitivity`, scoped down to answer in well under a second.
opt.noImprovement: The search didn't find anything that scores better than today's config over this symbol's cached history — nothing to propose.
opt.noRealYet: No closed trades for this symbol in the window being backtested.
opt.notEnough: Not enough cached history for {symbol} yet — let it run a while longer.
opt.notOverridable: Part of this win also depends on {fields} — shared engine/exits settings with no per-symbol override, so pasting the proposal above alone won't fully reproduce these numbers.
opt.proposedHint: Not applied automatically — review it, then add it under strategy_overrides in config.yaml yourself if it looks right.
opt.sub: which value of one field backtests best
opt.symbolIntro: Runs a bounded guided search plus a refine pass against one symbol's own cached history and proposes a strategy_overrides entry — the same question this was used to answer for GOOG and AMZN by hand, on demand. Never applied automatically.
opt.symbolSub: propose a per-symbol config from its own recent history
opt.title: Field optimizer
opt.totalContext: For context only, not compared — this symbol's all-time real track record: {trades} trades, {win} win rate, {expectancy} expectancy per trade.
opt.unknownField: That field has no tested values (nothing sweeps it yet).
pill.liveHelp: The event stream is down; data still refreshes by polling.
pos.holdingsSub: what the broker reports you own
pos.noDrift: The bot's records match the broker.
pos.noTracked: The bot is not tracking any open position.
pos.trackedSub: positions the bot opened and is managing
settings.ai.api_key.help: Bearer token for the openai provider. Ollama needs none.
settings.ai.api_key.label: API key
settings.ai.base_url.label: Base URL
settings.ai.blocking.help: Wait for the model instead of using the cache. Backtests only — never live.
settings.ai.blocking.label: Blocking
settings.ai.enabled.help: Build the advisor. Off means the ai detector always votes HOLD.
settings.ai.enabled.label: Enabled
settings.ai.intro: An LLM-backed opinion on the same readings the rule-based detectors vote on. It never blocks the trading loop, fails to HOLD, and its strength is capped.
settings.ai.max_age.help: Verdicts older than this are not used.
settings.ai.max_age.label: Max verdict age
settings.ai.max_concurrent.help: In-flight request cap; protects a single local GPU.
settings.ai.max_concurrent.label: Max concurrent
settings.ai.max_strength.help: Ceiling on the strength it contributes (0–1). Keep it low so the LLM tilts a decision rather than carrying one.
settings.ai.max_strength.label: Max strength
settings.ai.min_confidence.help: Below this, the model's own answer becomes HOLD.
settings.ai.min_confidence.label: Min confidence
settings.ai.model.help: e.g. llama3.2 — a small instruct model is plenty.
settings.ai.model.label: Model
settings.ai.provider.help: ollama = native API; openai = any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
settings.ai.provider.label: Provider
settings.ai.refresh_interval.help: Minimum time between calls for one symbol (15m).
settings.ai.refresh_interval.label: Refresh interval
settings.ai.system_prompt.help: Overrides the built-in instruction. Empty = the default, which asks for a strict JSON verdict.
settings.ai.system_prompt.label: System prompt
settings.ai.temperature.help: 0 is as reproducible as the model allows.
settings.ai.temperature.label: Temperature
settings.ai.timeout.label: Timeout
settings.ai.title: AI advisor
settings.autotune.bars.help: Candle window analyzed per symbol per run, taken from the end of whatever is cached. ~390 = one trading day at 1-min bars, ~1440 = one calendar day.
settings.autotune.bars.label: Bars per symbol
settings.autotune.danger: ⚠️ Unsupervised. When a run finds a config that beats a symbol's own backtest AND its real track record, it writes the result straight into strategy_overrides and the running engine — no confirmation step, no human in the loop. Watch the Strategy tab's manual "optimize this symbol" button produce sensible proposals for your own symbols before enabling this.
settings.autotune.enabled.help: Turn the scheduled job on. Off: nothing runs, nothing is ever written to strategy_overrides automatically. Enabling this for the FIRST TIME needs a restart — the background job is only started once, at startup, if this was already on.
settings.autotune.enabled.label: Enabled
settings.autotune.exclude_symbols.help: Keep specific symbols out of the scheduler's reach entirely — e.g. ones you've hand-tuned and don't want silently overwritten. Applied after "Only these symbols" below, so a symbol in both ends up excluded. Empty = nothing excluded.
settings.autotune.exclude_symbols.label: Exclude symbols
settings.autotune.interval.help: How often a pass runs (24h). Changing this needs a restart, same as the screener's own interval.
settings.autotune.interval.label: Interval
settings.autotune.intro: Runs the Strategy tab's per-symbol optimizer automatically on a schedule, against every eligible watchlist symbol.
settings.autotune.min_return_pct.help: Absolute floor on a proposal's own backtested return. Beating a weak or empty baseline is not the same as making money — a symbol with nothing to beat could otherwise let a lossmaking config through just for edging out a score of zero. 0 (the default) rejects any negative return; raise it for a stricter bar, or set it negative to deliberately tolerate a small loss.
settings.autotune.min_return_pct.label: Minimum return %
settings.autotune.min_trades.help: Reject a candidate config that only "worked" because it barely traded. Deliberately stricter than the manual button's own floor (3) — an unsupervised, every-symbol, real-money write deserves less tolerance for a thin sample.
settings.autotune.min_trades.label: Minimum trades
settings.autotune.objective.help: What "better" means when ranking candidate configs. blend = both return and win rate, penalising drawdown (the default). return = most earnings, whatever the win rate. winrate = most winning trades, whatever the earnings. sharpe/sortino/calmar = risk-adjusted. profitfactor/expectancy = trade quality regardless of position size. Whatever you pick, a proposal must still beat this symbol's real track record on win rate AND expectancy specifically — the only two numbers comparable between a backtest and real trading.
settings.autotune.objective.label: Optimize for
settings.autotune.on_loss.after_losses.h: Consecutive losing closes on one symbol that trigger a re-tune of that symbol. A winning or breakeven close resets its counter, so a symbol alternating wins and losses is never touched. 0 defaults to 3; below 2 is not recommended - one losing trade is noise.
settings.autotune.on_loss.after_losses.l: Losses in a row before re-tuning
settings.autotune.on_loss.cooldown.help: Minimum time between two re-tunes of the SAME symbol, measured from its last autotune apply. A streak that arrives inside the cooldown is dropped and the counter restarts. Empty or 0 = no cooldown.
settings.autotune.on_loss.cooldown.label: Re-tune cooldown per symbol
settings.autotune.on_loss.enabled.help: Re-tune a single symbol as soon as it loses this many times in a row, instead of waiting for the next scheduled pass. Needs autotune itself to be enabled. Uses the same gates as a scheduled run, so a streak decides when to look, never what is allowed to win.
settings.autotune.on_loss.enabled.label: Re-tune after a losing streak
settings.autotune.runStarted: Started — running in the background; check the diagnostics log for results.
settings.autotune.run_only_for_symbols.h: Restrict every pass to exactly these watchlist symbols. Empty = every watchlist symbol is eligible (subject to Exclude symbols below).
settings.autotune.title: Autotune
settings.behavior.confirm_buy.help: Consecutive agreeing evaluations required before buying. 1 = act at once.
settings.behavior.confirm_buy.label: Confirm buy
settings.behavior.confirm_sell.help: Consecutive agreeing evaluations required before selling.
settings.behavior.confirm_sell.label: Confirm sell
settings.behavior.intro: The churn damping: how long a position must be held before a strategy sell, and how many consecutive agreeing evaluations are needed to act.
settings.behavior.keep_interval.help: Minimum hold before a STRATEGY sell is allowed (2h, 0s = off). Protective exits still fire immediately.
settings.behavior.keep_interval.label: Keep interval
settings.behavior.title: Holding and confirmation
settings.costs.commission_flat.label: Commission flat
settings.costs.commission_min.label: Commission minimum
settings.costs.commission_pct.label: Commission %
settings.costs.intro: Folds the true cost of trading into order sizing, the money limits and backtest P&L.
settings.costs.measure_spread.help: Estimate each instrument's spread from its own bars (Corwin–Schultz) instead of applying one number to everything. The spread above stays a FLOOR — an estimate says the real cost is at least that much, never less. Measured values come from the screener.
settings.costs.measure_spread.label: Measure spread per symbol
settings.costs.slippage_pct.help: Extra adverse move per fill, as a fraction of price. The cost of size, latency and a moving market.
settings.costs.slippage_pct.label: Slippage
settings.costs.spread_pct.help: FULL spread as a fraction of price (0.0005 = 5 bps). Half is paid on every fill. Affects backtests and the simulated broker — a live venue charges what it charges.
settings.costs.spread_pct.label: Bid-ask spread
settings.costs.title: Trading costs
settings.entries.allow_pyramiding.help: Let repeated BUY signals add to a position already open. Off = at most one entry per symbol until it is exited.
settings.entries.allow_pyramiding.label: Allow pyramiding
settings.entries.danger: ⚠️ Scale-in is averaging down. It improves the entry price of every trade that recovers and increases the size of every trade that does not. Keep max_adds small, keep the stop-loss on, and prove it in a backtest before trusting it with money.
settings.entries.intro: When a new position — or an addition to one — may open.
settings.entries.scale_in.enabled.help: Average down on an explicit, capped schedule. Read the warning above first.
settings.entries.scale_in.enabled.label: Scale-in enabled
settings.entries.scale_in.max_adds.help: Hard cap on adds per position. Required — an uncapped ladder is a martingale.
settings.entries.scale_in.max_adds.label: Scale-in max adds
settings.entries.scale_in.require_signal: Only add while the strategy still says BUY. Without it, the ladder buys purely because the price fell — a mean-reversion bet the strategy never made.
settings.entries.scale_in.size_pct.help: Each add as a fraction of a normal order (1.0 = a full extra order). Above 1 is martingale sizing and is rejected.
settings.entries.scale_in.size_pct.label: Scale-in size
settings.entries.scale_in.step_pct.help: How far below the AVERAGE entry price before the next add (0.03 = 3% underwater). Each add pulls the average down, so every further add needs a further fall.
settings.entries.scale_in.step_pct.label: Scale-in step
settings.entries.skip_full_slots.help: When max_open_positions is reached, stop evaluating symbols that cannot be bought. Held symbols are still evaluated and their exits always run. Saves LLM and ML calls spent forming opinions the risk manager will refuse.
settings.entries.skip_full_slots.label: Skip full slots
settings.entries.title: Entries
settings.exits.atr_period.help: Lookback for the volatility-adaptive stops below. 0 defaults to 14.
settings.exits.atr_period.label: ATR period
settings.exits.atr_stop_mult.help: Place the stop this many ATRs below entry instead of a fixed percentage. The wider of the two wins, so the percentage acts as a floor. 0 = percentage only.
settings.exits.atr_stop_mult.label: ATR stop multiple
settings.exits.atr_trail_mult.help: The same idea for the trailing stop. 0 = percentage only.
settings.exits.atr_trail_mult.label: ATR trail multiple
settings.exits.bypass_trading_halt.help: Let stop-loss/trailing-stop/take-profit/max-hold/scale-out keep submitting REAL sell orders even while trading is off — a manual toggle, a protections halt, or a circuit breaker. Off (default): a halt freezes exits too, exactly like everything else. On: mirrors how a manual sell already always bypasses the toggle, so a stop-loss can still cap a loss during the very drawdown that tripped the halt. Only affects these automatic protective exits — strategy-driven entries/exits still fully respect the toggle either way.
settings.exits.bypass_trading_halt.label: Exits ignore a trading halt
settings.exits.enabled.help: Turn protective exits on or off. They run before strategy signals.
settings.exits.enabled.label: Exits enabled
settings.exits.intro: Checked before any strategy signal; a triggered exit always wins. Order of precedence: stop-loss → trailing stop → take-profit/ROI → max hold. The scale-out ladder only runs when none of them fired.
settings.exits.max_hold.help: Close unconditionally after this long, at whatever the market offers (72h, 0s = off). The ROI ladder can only exit at breakeven or better; nothing else closes a position that is simply dead money at a small loss while it occupies a slot.
settings.exits.max_hold.label: Max hold (time barrier)
settings.exits.partial_take_profit.help: Sell part of the position at successive gains, as profit:fraction pairs (0.05:0.33, 0.12:0.33). Each rung fires once; fractions are of the ORIGINAL size and must sum to 1 or less. This trades expectancy for variance — measure it in a backtest.
settings.exits.partial_take_profit.label: Scale-out ladder
settings.exits.roi.help: Time-decaying profit target as duration:fraction pairs, e.g. 0s:0.10, 30m:0.05, 2h:0.02, 6h:0. Demands a lot early and settles for less as a trade goes stale.
settings.exits.roi.label: ROI ladder
settings.exits.stop_loss_pct.help: Sell when price falls this fraction below entry (0.05 = 5%). 0 disables.
settings.exits.stop_loss_pct.label: Stop-loss
settings.exits.take_profit_pct.help: Sell when price rises this fraction above entry (0.20 = 20%). 0 disables.
settings.exits.take_profit_pct.label: Take-profit
settings.exits.title: Protective exits
settings.exits.trailing_offset_pct.help: Profit at which the trail switches to the tight distance (0.05 = +5%). One distance cannot be both loose enough early that noise does not end a trade and tight enough late that a winner is not handed back — so it is two. 0 disables the second stage.
settings.exits.trailing_offset_pct.label: Trail: tighten above
settings.exits.trailing_only_after_offse: Suppress trailing entirely below the offset, leaving only the stop-loss. Use when the trail exists to protect a gain, not to cap a loss.
settings.exits.trailing_stop_pct.help: Sell when price falls this fraction below the peak since entry. 0 disables.
settings.exits.trailing_stop_pct.label: Trailing stop
settings.exits.trailing_tight_pct.help: The trailing distance used once the offset is reached. It should be SMALLER than the ordinary trailing stop — that is the point.
settings.exits.trailing_tight_pct.label: Trail: tight distance
settings.limits.cash_reserve.help: Cash the bot may never spend.
settings.limits.cash_reserve.label: Cash reserve
settings.limits.cash_reserve_pct.help: Cash that must stay uninvested, as a fraction of current equity (0.05 = 5%). 0 = off. This one is a FLOOR, so if the fixed amount above is also set the LARGER of the two binds — the more conservative reserve wins.
settings.limits.cash_reserve_pct.label: Cash reserve (% of equity)
settings.limits.intro: The hard ceilings every order passes through. These are enforced before anything reaches a broker.
settings.limits.max_daily_spend.help: Ceiling on cash deployed per day, commission included.
settings.limits.max_daily_spend.label: Max daily spend
settings.limits.max_daily_spend_pct.help: Cap on cumulative buy notional within a rolling trading day, as a fraction of current equity. 0 = off. If the fixed amount above is also set, the tighter of the two binds.
settings.limits.max_open_positions.help: How many distinct symbols may be held at once. 0 = no cap.
settings.limits.max_open_positions.label: Max open positions
settings.limits.max_order_value.label: Max order value
settings.limits.max_order_value_pct.help: Cap on a single order's notional, as a fraction of current equity (0.20 = 20%). 0 = off. If the fixed amount above is also set, the tighter of the two binds.
settings.limits.max_per_position.help: Ceiling on any single symbol's market value.
settings.limits.max_per_position.label: Max per position
settings.limits.max_per_position_pct.hel: Cap on the market value held in any single symbol, as a fraction of current equity (0.20 = 20%). 0 = off. If the fixed amount above is also set, the tighter of the two binds.
settings.limits.max_total_invested.help: Ceiling on the combined market value of all positions.
settings.limits.max_total_invested.label: Max total invested
settings.limits.max_total_invested_pct.h: Cap on the total market value of all open positions, as a fraction of current equity (0.95 = 95%). Tracks the account as it grows, so you never have to edit the fixed amount. 0 = off. If the fixed amount above is also set, the tighter of the two binds.
settings.limits.title: Money limits
settings.ml.buy_prob.help: Probability at which it votes BUY (0.58).
settings.ml.buy_prob.label: Buy probability
settings.ml.enabled.help: Build the predictor. Off means the ml detector always votes HOLD.
settings.ml.enabled.label: Enabled
settings.ml.epochs.label: Epochs
settings.ml.horizon.help: How many bars ahead the label looks.
settings.ml.horizon.label: Horizon (bars)
settings.ml.intro: A logistic regression over the same normalised readings, retrained on a rolling window. Every prediction is out-of-sample. It will usually find very little — min_skill exists to make a model that learned nothing say so.
settings.ml.l2.help: Ridge penalty — the main brake on overfitting the window.
settings.ml.l2.label: L2 penalty
settings.ml.learning_rate.label: Learning rate
settings.ml.max_strength.help: Ceiling on the strength it contributes (0–1).
settings.ml.max_strength.label: Max strength
settings.ml.min_samples.help: Fewest labelled rows needed to fit at all.
settings.ml.min_samples.label: Min samples
settings.ml.min_skill.help: Required accuracy ABOVE the majority-class base rate (0.02 = 2pp) before it may vote. The guard against acting on a model that learned nothing.
settings.ml.min_skill.label: Min skill
settings.ml.retrain_every.help: Refit cadence in BARS, so backtest and live agree.
settings.ml.retrain_every.label: Retrain every (bars)
settings.ml.sell_prob.help: Probability at which it votes SELL (0.42). Must be below the buy probability.
settings.ml.sell_prob.label: Sell probability
settings.ml.threshold.help: Forward return counting as up (0.005 = 0.5%). 0 asks whether price ticked up, which after costs is not a tradeable question.
settings.ml.threshold.label: Label threshold
settings.ml.title: ML detector
settings.ml.train_bars.help: Rolling window the model is fitted on.
settings.ml.train_bars.label: Training window (bars)
settings.notify.apprise_services.help: Stateless mode only: comma-separated Apprise service URLs.
settings.notify.apprise_services.label: Apprise services
settings.notify.apprise_tag.help: Stored config only: which entries to notify.
settings.notify.apprise_tag.label: Apprise tag
settings.notify.apprise_url.label: Apprise API URL
settings.notify.discord_webhook.label: Discord webhook
settings.notify.enabled.label: Enabled
settings.notify.events.help: Which kinds to send: trade, halt, error, blocked (blocked is noisy).
settings.notify.events.label: Events
settings.notify.intro: Outbound alerts. Delivery is queued and droppable, so a slow sink can never stall trading. Secrets are shown redacted; leave them untouched to keep the stored value.
settings.notify.min_notional.help: Suppress fill alerts below this order value. Halts and errors are always sent.
settings.notify.min_notional.label: Min notional
settings.notify.pushover_device.help: Optional: restrict to one device name.
settings.notify.pushover_device.label: Pushover device
settings.notify.pushover_priority.help: -2 silent, -1 quiet, 0 normal, 1 high. Halts and errors go one level higher, capped at 1.
settings.notify.pushover_priority.label: Pushover priority
settings.notify.pushover_token.label: Pushover app token
settings.notify.pushover_user.label: Pushover user key
settings.notify.telegram_chat_id.help: The chat or group to post into.
settings.notify.telegram_chat_id.label: Telegram chat ID
settings.notify.telegram_token.label: Telegram bot token
settings.notify.timeout.label: Timeout
settings.notify.title: Notifications
settings.notify.webhook.help: Any URL — receives the event as a JSON POST.
settings.notify.webhook.label: Webhook URL
settings.persistence: Changes apply immediately and are written back to config.yaml in place — only the edited values change; your comments and layout are kept. Anything that fails to save says so.
settings.portfolio.asset_classes.help: name:value pairs, e.g. IWDA.AS:etf, SAP.DE:stock. Values: stock, etf, fund, bond, crypto, option, future, cfd, currency, index. Filled in automatically from the data provider (and the broker's instrument list); entries here override that. A symbol nothing can classify is budgeted under "unclassified", so it is capped only if you give that class a share.
settings.portfolio.asset_classes.label: Asset class map
Bars to measure correlation over. 0 defaults to 200. Too short is noise; too long describes a regime that has passed.
settings.portfolio.correlation_threshold: Above this, two symbols count as the same bet (0.8 is a reasonable start).
settings.portfolio.enabled.help: Master switch for the concentration caps.
settings.portfolio.enabled.label: Enabled
settings.portfolio.intro: Concentration caps across the whole book. The per-order money limits will happily let the bot hold twenty positions that are really one bet.
settings.portfolio.max_correlated_positi: How many held symbols may exceed that threshold. 0 = no cap.
settings.portfolio.max_pct_per_asset_cla: name:value pairs as a FRACTION of equity, e.g. etf:0.6, stock:0.3. Classes: stock, etf, fund, bond, crypto, option, future, cfd, currency, index, plus "unclassified" for everything the bot could not place. An absent class is uncapped. Once a class is at its share of the book, further buys in it are refused - including topping up a position already held. Sells and exits are never affected.
settings.portfolio.max_per_sector.help: Combined market value allowed in one sector label. 0 = no cap.
settings.portfolio.max_per_sector.label: Max value per sector
settings.portfolio.max_positions_per_sec: Distinct symbols allowed in one sector. 0 = no cap.
settings.portfolio.min_positions_per_ass: name:count pairs, e.g. stock:2, etf:3. A class WITH a share above gets that share of the investable book split n ways: stock:2 against a 0.7 share of a 1000 book (less a 50 cash reserve) means no single stock position may exceed 332.50. A class without a share gets an equal cut of whatever the named shares did not claim. A class not named here falls back to whatever Min positions has left over. A ceiling, not a floor: it never makes the bot buy.
settings.portfolio.sector_caps_per_asset: Count the two sector caps WITHIN each asset class instead of across the whole book, so a tech ETF and a tech stock no longer compete for the same slot. On means "N single-stock bets AND N diversified bets per sector" - defensible because a sector ETF holds dozens of companies while a stock holds one, and the asset-class caps already bound each wrapper. Off (the default) is the stricter reading: a sector falls together whatever wrapper it comes in. The screener's max_symbols_per_sector follows this setting, so selection and enforcement agree.
Count sector caps per asset class
settings.portfolio.sectors.help: name:value pairs, e.g. AAPL:tech, MSFT:tech, XOM:energy. Unmapped symbols skip the sector caps but not the correlation check.
settings.portfolio.sectors.label: Sector map
settings.portfolio.title: Portfolio limits
settings.protections.cooldown_after_loss: No new entry in a symbol for this long after a losing exit (30m, 2h, 0s = off).
settings.protections.drop_after_losses.h: Remove a symbol from the watchlist entirely after this many CONSECUTIVE losing closes, and comment its entry out of config.yaml so the removal survives a restart. The other guards here lock a symbol out and then let it back in; this is the one that gives up. A winning or breakeven close resets the count. A symbol with an OPEN POSITION is never dropped - that would strand it with no exits - so it waits for the position to close. The config entry is commented, not deleted, so the symbol and the reason stay in the file and undoing it is removing one '#'. Set it well above autotune.on_loss.after_losses if you use both. 0 = never.
settings.protections.drop_after_losses.l: Drop from watchlist after N losses
settings.protections.enabled.help: Master switch for the outcome-driven circuit breakers.
settings.protections.enabled.label: Enabled
settings.protections.intro: Circuit breakers that watch outcomes over time. They gate ENTRIES only — an exit is never blocked — and a halt is sticky until deliberately resumed.
settings.protections.low_profit_lock.hel: How long the symbol is then locked out of new entries (24h).
settings.protections.low_profit_lookback: The window those trades must fall within (168h = 7 days).
Realised profit the window must clear, in account currency. 0 = must at least break even.
settings.protections.low_profit_trades.h: How many closed trades in ONE symbol are judged. 0 = off. Catches what the stop guard cannot: a symbol that trips no stop and moves the account very little, but bleeds commission and spread.
Halt after losing this much of the day's starting equity (0.08 = 8%).
settings.protections.max_drawdown_pct.he: Halt ALL automated trading this far below the equity peak (0.20 = 20%). Sticky until resumed. Counts EVERYTHING, including unrealized paper losses on positions still held — a heavy-exposure period with an ordinary market dip can trip this well before any position is actually sold at a loss.
settings.protections.max_realized_drawdo: Halt ALL automated trading once cumulative REALIZED P&L (closed trades only) has given back this much of the account's peak equity since its own high (0.15 = 15%). Ignores unrealized mark-to-market swings entirely — only money actually locked in by a closed trade counts. Independent of the drawdown above: set either, both, or neither. 0 disables it.
settings.protections.stop_guard_lock.hel: How long the symbol is then locked out (4h).
settings.protections.stop_guard_lookback: The window those stop-outs must fall within (24h).
settings.protections.stop_guard_trades.h: How many protective stop-outs of ONE symbol trip the guard. 0 = off.
settings.protections.title: Protections
settings.screener.enabled.help: Maintain the watchlist automatically. Off = the watchlist is whatever config and the API say.
settings.screener.enabled.label: Enabled
settings.screener.filters.help: Which checks to run, in order: history, price, volume, volatility, spread. Evaluation stops at the first failure, so a verdict names the binding constraint. EMPTY = all of them, default order.
settings.screener.filters.label: Filter chain
settings.screener.interval.help: How often to re-screen (6h). Changing this needs a restart; the filters themselves take effect on the next pass.
settings.screener.interval.label: Interval
settings.screener.intro: Automatic universe selection. Symbols you hold are never dropped — that would strand the position with no exits.
settings.screener.keep_held.help: Only changes how a held symbol that fails the filters is labeled in the screener's own history ("kept" vs "would have failed"). Held symbols are never actually dropped from the watchlist either way — see the note above.
settings.screener.keep_held.label: Keep held symbols
settings.screener.keep_manual.help: Never drop a symbol you chose yourself, and don't count it against the maximum. The screener then only adds — its own picks stay temporary.
settings.screener.keep_manual.label: Only ever add to my watchlist
settings.screener.lookback_days.help: How much history to pull per candidate. Must be long enough that the bar size yields more than min_history_bars - daily bars over 30 days is about 20 observations, which cannot support an ATR let alone a trend fit, so a daily profile wants a year.
settings.screener.lookback_days.label: History window (days)
settings.screener.max_drawdown_pct.help: Reject a candidate whose own peak-to-trough decline over the window exceeds this fraction (0.30 = 30%). A falling knife passes a volatility band and can pass momentum on a dead-cat bounce; this is what refuses it. 0 = no bound. Needs "drawdown" in the filter chain.
settings.screener.max_drawdown_pct.label: Max own drawdown
settings.screener.max_price.label: Max price
settings.screener.max_spread_pct.help: Drop instruments whose estimated bid-ask spread exceeds this fraction of price (0.005 = 50 bps). Paid twice per round trip and invisible on a chart — a symbol can look tradeable and still be unable to clear its own cost of entry. 0 = no bound.
settings.screener.max_spread_pct.label: Max spread
settings.screener.max_symbols.help: Keep the best N by rank. 0 = all survivors.
settings.screener.max_symbols.label: Max symbols
settings.screener.max_symbols_per_sector: How many SELECTED symbols may share a sector label. The screener ranks on trend or volume, which correlate hard within an industry, so without this it fills every slot with one sector - and the portfolio guard then refuses most of those buys at order time, after you have paid for the feed subscription and warmup. Set it to the portfolio's max_positions_per_sector, or a little above so a closing position has a replacement ready. Counted across all asset classes. Held and pinned symbols are exempt. 0 = no cap.
settings.screener.max_volatility_pct.hel: Too wild is unsurvivable. 0 = no bound.
settings.screener.min_avg_volume.help: Drop thin instruments. European ETF listings often trade far below US-style thresholds.
settings.screener.min_avg_volume.label: Min average volume
settings.screener.min_cost_multiple.help: Require the typical bar-to-bar move to be at least this many times the instrument's own round trip (two spreads plus commission). Decides whether it can pay for being traded at all: something moving 0.1% a bar against a 0.15% round trip loses at every win rate. 3 is a sensible floor, 0 = no bound. Needs "cost" in the filter chain.
settings.screener.min_history_bars.help: Never trade something the strategy cannot warm up on.
settings.screener.min_history_bars.label: Min history (bars)
settings.screener.min_price.label: Min price
settings.screener.min_trend_r2.help: How well price must fit a straight line over the window, 0..1. Separates a clean advance from a sideways chop that happens to end higher - momentum alone cannot tell them apart. 0 = no bound. Needs "trend" in the filter chain.
settings.screener.min_trend_r2.label: Min trend quality (R²)
settings.screener.min_trend_slope_pct.he: How fast that fitted line must rise, as a fraction of price per bar. Pairs with R²: R² says the trend is clean, slope says it is worth having. 0 = no bound.
settings.screener.min_volatility_pct.hel: Too quiet is untradeable after costs. 0 = no bound.
settings.screener.probe.autotune.help: Also run the bounded per-symbol search to find the candidate's BEST configuration. Answers "could this work if I tuned for it?", which finds symbols your current settings happen to suit badly - but that number is only achievable if you then tune for it. Much slower.
settings.screener.probe.autotune.label: Probe with a parameter search
settings.screener.probe.backtest.help: Run your current strategy over each shortlisted candidate. Answers "would what I am running now have worked here?" - the honest question for adopting a symbol into a book that trades one configuration.
settings.screener.probe.backtest.label: Probe with the live strategy
settings.screener.probe.enabled.help: After the filters, actually trade the best survivors in a backtest before adopting them. The filters establish that an instrument is tradeable; this establishes whether trading it would have made money. Costs real time on every pass.
settings.screener.probe.enabled.label: Backtest the shortlist
settings.screener.probe.max_candidates.h: How many survivors per asset class reach the probe, taken best-first from the cheap ranking. A candidate beyond the cutoff keeps its ranking - not probed is not the same as probed badly. 0 defaults to 10.
settings.screener.probe.min_expectancy_p: Reject a candidate whose probe expectancy per trade falls below this fraction. 0 rejects anything that does not at least break even; negative tolerates a small loss; below -1 scores without ever rejecting.
settings.screener.probe.min_trades.help: Ignore a probe result built on fewer trades than this; the candidate keeps its cheap-filter ranking instead of being judged on a handful of lucky fills. The result is still recorded so you can see why. 0 defaults to 5.
settings.screener.probe.min_trades.label: Min probe trades to trust
settings.screener.rank.help: How survivors are ordered before the cap is applied.
settings.screener.rank.label: Rank by
settings.screener.resolution.help: Which candles candidates are measured on: 1, 5, 15, 60 minutes or D (daily). The most type-dependent setting there is - a broad ETF judged on 1-minute bars is measured on noise, while the same bars are right for a liquid megacap. Override per asset class in config.yaml.
settings.screener.resolution.label: Bar size to judge on
settings.screener.suggest_universe.help: Fill any asset class with no universe of your own from a built-in starter pool of liquid, widely available instruments. Turn this on if you want the screener to find things but do not yet know what to list - an empty universe makes it filter-only, able to drop symbols but never find any. A starting point, not a recommendation: nothing in it skips a filter.
settings.screener.suggest_universe.label: Seed with suggested symbols
settings.screener.title: Screener
settings.screener.universe.help: Candidate symbols to screen. EMPTY = filter the current watchlist and never add to it.
settings.screener.universe.label: Universe
settings.sizing.intro: How large a buy is before the money limits clamp it.
settings.sizing.max_risk_size_usd.help: Cap on what risk-based sizing may produce, so a very tight stop can't translate into an oversized position. 0 = only the money limits apply.
settings.sizing.max_risk_size_usd.label: Max risk-sized order
settings.sizing.min_order_size_usd.help: Smallest order worth placing. If risk scaling puts an order below this, the order is REFUSED rather than rounded up — raising it would enlarge exactly the trades the scaling just judged too risky to hold at full size. 0 = no threshold.
settings.sizing.min_order_size_usd.label: Min order size
settings.sizing.min_positions.help: Spread the budget over at least this many positions, so no single buy takes more than its share of what can actually be invested (equity less cash_reserve, capped at max_total_invested). 0 = no global split. The per-asset-class split on the Portfolio tab refines this and wins for the classes it names.
settings.sizing.min_positions.label: Min positions
settings.sizing.title: Position sizing
settings.test_mode.danger: ⚠️ While active, EVERY order — automated or manual — is routed to an internal simulated broker instead of the real one, regardless of the trading toggle above. Nothing placed during this window touches the real account.
settings.test_mode.duration.help: How long a training window stays active before it auto-ends and real orders resume. 0 falls back to 48h.
settings.test_mode.duration.label: Duration
settings.test_mode.enabled.help: Start a training window automatically every time the bot starts. Off: the bot starts trading (or dry-running) for real immediately, as before this feature existed.
settings.test_mode.enabled.label: Enabled by default at startup
settings.test_mode.intro: A simulated "training phase": the engine keeps reading real market data and running its normal strategy/risk/exits loop, but every order fills against an internal simulated broker seeded from the real account's cash and positions — so simulated trades feed the autotune's own track-record gating without ever touching the real account.
settings.test_mode.title: Test mode
settings.title: Settings
strategy.adx_period.help: Lookback for the Average Directional Index (trend strength). Needs roughly twice this many bars.
strategy.adx_period.label: ADX period
strategy.adx_threshold.help: Minimum ADX to treat the move as a trend (e.g. 25); +DI versus −DI sets the direction.
strategy.adx_threshold.label: ADX threshold
strategy.atr_mult.help: Breakout trigger: a move beyond this multiple of ATR versus the prior close.
strategy.atr_mult.label: ATR multiple
strategy.atr_period.label: ATR period
strategy.bb_period.help: Window for the Bollinger midline (a simple moving average).
strategy.bb_period.label: Bollinger period
strategy.bb_stddev.help: Standard-deviation multiplier for the bands. Buys below the lower band, sells above the upper.
strategy.bb_stddev.label: Bollinger σ
strategy.combine.help: majority = act on the side with more votes; unanimous = all must agree; weighted = act on the net strength-weighted score.
strategy.combine.label: Combine mode (buy)
strategy.combine_sell.help: Merge mode for SELL only. Empty = same as buy. Setting this to unanimous makes exits STRICTER than entries, which is rarely what you want.
strategy.combine_sell.label: Combine mode (sell)
strategy.deny_breakout_period.help: Short lookback (bars) for the false-breakout check: denies a BUY at a fresh high on unconfirmed volume. 0 disables just this check.
strategy.deny_breakout_period.label: Deny gate: breakout lookback (bars)
strategy.deny_breakout_rvol_period.help: Relative-volume lookback for the same check. 0 falls back to the breakout period.
strategy.deny_breakout_rvol_period.label: Deny gate: breakout RVOL lookback (bars)
strategy.deny_breakout_rvol_threshold.he: Minimum relative volume a fresh high must show to be trusted as a real breakout; below it, the buy is denied.
strategy.deny_gate.help: Short-term veto checked only on a BUY that already passed everything else: denies a false breakout or an already-overextended move. SELL is never denied.
strategy.deny_gate.label: Deny gate
strategy.deny_reversal_overbought.help: %K level, on the short lookback below, past which a buy is denied as chasing an already-extended move.
strategy.deny_reversal_overbought.label: Deny gate: reversal overbought (%K)
strategy.deny_reversal_stoch_period.help: Short %K lookback (bars) for the overextension check. 0 disables just this check.
strategy.detectors.help: Comma-separated indicators for BUY decisions. The ai detector asks an LLM about the same readings; the ml detector uses a learned model. Both hold unless configured.
strategy.detectors.label: Buy detectors
strategy.detectorsSub: every detector's current call, including inactive ones (• marks the active set)
strategy.detectors_sell.help: Indicators for SELL decisions. Empty reuses the buy detectors.
strategy.detectors_sell.label: Sell detectors
strategy.donchian_period.help: Lookback for the Donchian breakout channel — highest high and lowest low (e.g. 20).
strategy.donchian_period.label: Donchian period
strategy.fast_ma.help: Short EMA period for the trend crossover. Must be smaller than the slow EMA.
strategy.fast_ma.label: Fast EMA
strategy.healthSub: realized track record and protection-lock state per traded symbol, all time
strategy.maOrder: fast_ma must be smaller than slow_ma.
strategy.macd_fast.label: MACD fast
strategy.macd_signal.help: MACD signal-line EMA period (e.g. 9). Buys when the histogram is positive.
strategy.macd_signal.label: MACD signal
strategy.macd_slow.label: MACD slow
strategy.min_strength.help: Minimum combined confidence to BUY. Higher means fewer, higher-conviction entries.
strategy.min_strength.label: Min strength — buy
strategy.min_strength_sell.help: Minimum confidence to SELL. -1 = same as buy. Set lower to exit more readily than you enter.
strategy.min_strength_sell.label: Min strength — sell
strategy.noOverrides: No symbol has its own strategy parameters — every symbol trades on the shared config above.
strategy.overridesSub: symbols trading on their own parameters (strategy_overrides in config.yaml) — read-only, edit config.yaml to change
strategy.rsi_mode.help: midline = graded vote around 50 (always participates); extremes = only votes at oversold/overbought.
strategy.rsi_mode.label: RSI mode
strategy.rsi_overbought.help: RSI level treated as overbought, producing sell pressure (e.g. 70).
strategy.rsi_overbought.label: RSI overbought
strategy.rsi_oversold.help: RSI level treated as oversold, producing buy pressure (e.g. 30).
strategy.rsi_oversold.label: RSI oversold
strategy.rsi_period.help: Lookback for the RSI momentum oscillator.
strategy.rsi_period.label: RSI period
strategy.rvol_period.help: Window for average volume in Relative Volume.
strategy.rvol_period.label: RVOL period
strategy.rvol_threshold.help: Volume surge needed to confirm a move (1.5 = 150% of average).
strategy.rvol_threshold.label: RVOL threshold
strategy.slow_ma.help: Long EMA period. ema_cross is bullish when fast is above slow.
strategy.slow_ma.label: Slow EMA
strategy.stoch_d_period.help: Smoothing period for %D (a moving average of %K).
strategy.stoch_d_period.label: Stochastic %D period
strategy.stoch_k_period.help: Lookback for Stochastic %K (position within the high/low range).
strategy.stoch_k_period.label: Stochastic %K period
strategy.stoch_overbought.help: %K at or above this is overbought, producing sell pressure (e.g. 80).
strategy.stoch_overbought.label: Stochastic overbought
strategy.stoch_oversold.help: %K at or below this is oversold, producing buy pressure (e.g. 20).
strategy.stoch_oversold.label: Stochastic oversold
strategy.supertrend_mult.help: ATR multiple for the Supertrend band (e.g. 3). Larger means fewer flips.
strategy.supertrend_mult.label: Supertrend multiplier
strategy.supertrend_period.help: ATR lookback for the Supertrend band (e.g. 10).
strategy.supertrend_period.label: Supertrend ATR period
strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.trend_gate.help: When on, the prevailing trend filters trades: an up-trend blocks SELLs and a down-trend blocks BUYs. Protective exits still fire.
strategy.trend_gate.label: Trend gate
strategy.trend_period.help: Bars for the regression trend, up to about a week. Reads the prevailing direction instead of the last bar or two.
strategy.trend_period.label: Trend lookback (bars)
strategy.trend_period_sell.help: Overrides the lookback used only when the gate is blocking a SELL (an up-trend). 0 = same as the buy-side lookback.
strategy.trend_period_sell.label: Trend lookback — sell
strategy.trend_threshold.help: Minimum end-to-end move of the fitted line to count as a trend (0.01 = 1%). Smaller moves are treated as flat.
strategy.trend_threshold.label: Trend threshold
strategy.trend_threshold_sell.help: Overrides the threshold used only when the gate is blocking a SELL (an up-trend). 0 = same as the buy-side threshold.
strategy.trend_threshold_sell.label: Trend threshold — sell
strategy.vp_buckets.help: Number of price bins in the profile.
strategy.vp_buckets.label: Volume-profile buckets
strategy.vp_value_area_pct.help: Fraction of volume around the point of control (0.7 = 70%).
strategy.vp_value_area_pct.label: Value-area share
strategy.vp_window.help: Bars used to build the volume profile.
strategy.vp_window.label: Volume-profile window
strategy.vwap_period.help: Rolling window for the volume-weighted average price (trend bias).
strategy.vwap_period.label: VWAP window
strategy.weights.help: Optional per-detector multipliers as name:weight pairs (trend:2, rsi:0.5). Missing detectors default to 1.
strategy.weights.label: Detector weights
trades.logSub: filled, dry-run, blocked and failed decisions
trades.noClosed: No closed trades in this period.
validate.duration: Must be a Go duration such as 30m, 2h or 0s. There is no day unit — use 72h, not 3d.
validate.rungFraction: Each rung's fraction must be between 0 and 1.
validate.rungTotal: The rungs sell {total}% of the position; they must sum to 100% or less.
validate.rungs: Write rungs as profit:fraction pairs, e.g. 0.05:0.33, 0.12:0.33.
watch.autoHint: Found by the screener. A later pass may drop it again — add it by hand to keep it.
watch.autotuneExcludedHint: Excluded from the scheduled auto-optimizer (autotune.exclude_symbols) — it will never be evaluated or have its strategy_overrides changed automatically.
watch.autotuneRunOnlyHint: Autotune is currently restricted to ONLY this (and possibly other) symbols named in autotune.run_only_for_symbols — every symbol not on that list is skipped by the scheduler until the restriction is removed.
watch.brokerLacksHint: Your broker has no instrument for this listing, so an order for it would be refused. You can still track it.
watch.classHint: Asset class — the bucket portfolio.max_pct_per_asset_class and the screener's per-class profile use for this symbol. Classified automatically; override it in config.yaml's asset_classes: block.
watch.lossStreakHint: Consecutive losing closes. At {of} in a row this symbol is re-tuned automatically (autotune.on_loss). A winning or breakeven close resets the count.
watch.refusedHint: The broker refuses orders for this instrument, so the bot has stopped trying. Remove it from the watchlist if that is permanent.
watch.runOnlyActive: Autotune is restricted to only: {symbols}. Every other watchlist symbol is skipped by the scheduler until this restriction is removed.
watch.screenerSub: why each candidate is or is not traded
watch.searchPlaceholder: Search by company name, e.g. Lanxess
watch.sectorHint: Sector — the bucket portfolio.max_positions_per_sector and the screener's max_symbols_per_sector use. Learned from the data provider unless config.yaml's sectors: block names it.
watch.sub: symbols the bot tracks and may trade
watch.title: Watchlist
